def solve(grid):
    n_rows = len(grid)
    n_cols = len(grid[0]) if n_rows else 0

    # ---- find the line colour (the colour that makes full rows/columns) ----
    full_row_colors = {}
    for r in range(n_rows):
        if len(set(grid[r])) == 1:
            c = grid[r][0]
            full_row_colors[c] = full_row_colors.get(c, 0) + 1

    full_col_colors = {}
    for c in range(n_cols):
        col_vals = [grid[r][c] for r in range(n_rows)]
        if len(set(col_vals)) == 1:
            ccol = col_vals[0]
            full_col_colors[ccol] = full_col_colors.get(ccol, 0) + 1

    # the line colour appears in at least one full row and one full column
    line_color = None
    for col in full_row_colors:
        if col in full_col_colors:
            line_color = col
            break
    if line_color is None:
        # fallback: just pick the colour that forms the most full rows
        line_color = max(full_row_colors, key=lambda x: full_row_colors[x])

    # ---- locate all full line rows and columns ----
    horiz_lines = [i for i in range(n_rows) if all(v == line_color for v in grid[i])]
    vert_lines = [j for j in range(n_cols) if all(grid[i][j] == line_color for i in range(n_rows))]

    # ---- choose the vertical interval ----
    # we need at least one column on each side, so we require width > 1
    if len(vert_lines) == 0:
        # should not happen – no vertical line
        L, R = -1, n_cols
        left_is_line = right_is_line = False
    else:
        first_v = vert_lines[0]
        if first_v > 1:                         # interval between border and first line is wide enough
            L, R = -1, first_v
            left_is_line, right_is_line = False, True
        else:
            # need to use interval between first and second line (if exists)
            if len(vert_lines) >= 2:
                L, R = vert_lines[0], vert_lines[1]
                left_is_line = right_is_line = True
            else:
                # only one vertical line, use interval after it (right side)
                L, R = vert_lines[0], n_cols
                left_is_line, right_is_line = True, False

    # width of the whole interval (excluding the line columns themselves)
    width = R - L - 1
    n_vert = len(vert_lines)

    # ---- compute effective width after cropping adjacent columns ----
    if left_is_line and right_is_line:
        # both sides are lines
        effective_width = width - 2 * (n_vert - 1)
    else:
        # only one side has a line
        sub = 1
        if n_vert == 1:
            sub += 1               # also treat the border side as a line when there is only one vertical line
        effective_width = width - sub

    # ---- build horizontal intervals ----
    intervals = []   # each entry: (start, end, top_is_line, bottom_is_line)
    prev = -1
    for h in horiz_lines:
        start = prev + 1
        end = h               # exclusive: row h is a line row
        top_is_line = (prev != -1)
        bottom_is_line = True
        intervals.append((start, end, top_is_line, bottom_is_line))
        prev = h
    # last interval after the last horizontal line
    start = prev + 1
    end = n_rows
    top_is_line = (prev != -1)
    bottom_is_line = False
    intervals.append((start, end, top_is_line, bottom_is_line))

    # ---- evaluate each interval ----
    best_area = -1
    best_idx = 0
    for idx, (s, e, top_line, bot_line) in enumerate(intervals):
        h = e - s
        if top_line and bot_line:
            effective_height = h - 2
        else:
            effective_height = h
        if effective_height <= 0:
            area = 0
        else:
            area = effective_width * effective_height

        # if we are in the "both‑sides line" case we may only consider intervals that start at the top border
        if left_is_line and right_is_line:
            if top_line:   # this interval does NOT start at the top border
                continue
        # choose the interval with the largest area, tie‑break by topmost (smaller start)
        if area > best_area or (area == best_area and s < intervals[best_idx][0]):
            best_area = area
            best_idx = idx

    # ---- unpack chosen interval ----
    s, e, top_line, bot_line = intervals[best_idx]

    # ---- compute final rows after removing adjacent rows ----
    row_start = s
    row_end = e          # exclusive
    if top_line:
        row_start += 1
    if bot_line:
        row_end -= 1

    # ---- compute final columns after removing adjacent columns ----
    col_start = L + 1    # first column inside the interval
    col_end = R          # exclusive (R is a line column)
    # determine how many columns to drop on each side
    if left_is_line and right_is_line:
        left_drop = right_drop = n_vert - 1
    else:
        # exactly one side has a line
        if n_vert == 1:
            left_drop = right_drop = 1
        else:
            if right_is_line:
                right_drop = 1
                left_drop = 0
            else:
                left_drop = 1
                right_drop = 0

    col_start += left_drop
    col_end   -= right_drop

    # ---- build the output grid ----
    out = []
    for r in range(row_start, row_end):
        row = []
        for c in range(col_start, col_end):
            row.append(grid[r][c])
        out.append(row)

    return out
